summary: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Cambridge funds outstanding young Africans for a one-year master's degree, with leadership training and a network that continues after graduation. The 2026–27 cohort had 69 scholars from 18 countries.
covers: Full funding for a one-year master's at Cambridge: fees and a maintenance allowance.
Leadership development and a 'Transition Project' linking your studies to work back home.
eligibility: Citizens of African countries with a strong academic record and financial need.
A commitment to contributing to Africa's development — the programme is built around returning to lead change.
Admission to an eligible Cambridge master's course; read the programme's eligibility page for course and age details.
how_to_apply: Choose an eligible one-year master's course and apply through Cambridge's graduate application portal, selecting the Mastercard Foundation scholarship.
Applications for 2027–28 opened on 11 September 2026 and close on 5 January 2027 (some courses close earlier).
If your country is not on the automatic application-fee-waiver list, submit the fee-waiver request form by 18 November 2026.
Shortlisted applicants are interviewed in the spring.
watch_out: Course deadlines can be earlier than the scholarship deadline — check your course page.
The fee-waiver request (18 November) comes well before the application deadline.
Your statement should connect your course to a concrete plan for impact in your community.

sources.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Cambridge
